assumptions.original: The coordinate index set is finite with decidable equality. The ambient measure is finite. Brownian motion is standard relative to the filtration, and the filtration satisfies the usual conditions. The initial coordinates are strongly measurable for the time-zero sigma algebra. The drift coordinates are strongly progressive with almost surely integrable time sections. The Brownian integrands are progressive and square-integrable on the horizon. The process stays on the unit sphere for every time in the horizon on a common full-measure event. A sphere point supplies a measurable fallback for exceptional samples in the compact Itô construction. The test is $C^2$ at each sphere point. The deterministic temperature is continuous and nonnegative on the horizon. The vector field evaluated along the process has almost surely continuous time paths. Almost surely throughout the horizon the drift is $-u_s-\lambda_s(d-1)X_s$ and the $j$th noise column is $\sqrt{2\lambda_s}(e_j-(X_s)_jX_s)$.
assumptions.reconstructed: B starts at zero for every omega, has jointly independent increments over disjoint half-open intervals, every continuous real linear functional ell sends B_t-B_s (s<t) to a centered Gaussian of variance (t-s)||ell||², and paths are continuous mu-a.e. B is strongly adapted to F and B_t-B_s is independent of F_s for s≤t. F is right-continuous and every subset S⊆Omega with mu(S)=0 belongs to F_t for every t≥0. A progressive L² integrand is a real process a(t,omega), strongly progressive for F, for which (omega,t)↦a(t,omega) is in L²(mu⊗lambda_T). Each x_i is strongly measurable for F_0; every b_i is strongly progressive and lambda_T-integrable pathwise mu-a.e. f is ambient C² at every unit vector. u has continuous paths on [0,T] mu-a.e. a is continuous on [0,T] and nonnegative at every t≤T. Let d=card(I) dotminus 1 in N, then cast to R. For mu-a.e. omega and all t≤T, ||X(t,omega)||=1. For mu-a.e. omega and all t≤T, (b_i(t,omega))_i=-u(t,omega)-a(t)d X(t,omega). For mu-a.e. omega, all t≤T and all j∈I, (eta_ij(t,omega))_i=sqrt(2a(t))(e_j-X_j(t,omega)X(t,omega)).

conclusion.original: On a positive finite horizon $[0,T]$, form the Euclidean process $X$ from its initial vector, progressive drift integral and completed Brownian coordinate integrals. Assume the process stays on the unit sphere almost surely throughout the horizon. If its drift and noise columns have the spherical coefficients below, then the increment of a twice continuously differentiable ambient test equals the time integral of the sphere generator plus the terminal value of a martingale starting at zero. Formula: f(X_T)-f(X_0)=\int_0^T\big[-Df(X_s)[u_s]+\lambda_s\Delta_{S^{d-1}}^{\rm ext} f(X_s)\big]\,ds+M_T\quad\text{almost surely}.
conclusion.reconstructed: I_j(a)(t,omega) denotes the specified completed Ito integral driven by the scalar coordinate B^j(t,omega)=(B(t,omega))_j. Its representative is the pointwise limit of chosen elementary stochastic integrals off the null complement of their uniform Cauchy event, and zero on that complement; it is held constant after T. Define X_i(t,omega)=x_i(omega)+∫b_i(s,omega)d lambda_t(s)+∑_j I_j(eta_ij)(t,omega). Define Lf(w)=Δf(w)-D²f(w)[w,w]-d Df(w)[w], with Δ=Laplacian.laplacian and natural truncated subtraction in d. Then there exists a real F-martingale M under mu, M(0,omega)=0 for every omega, such that mu-a.e.: f(X(T))-f(X(0))=∫[-Df(X(s))[u(s)]+a(s)Lf(X(s))]d lambda_T(s)+M(T).
